idea: US national parks and hiking trails
notes: Data: NPS API + open trail data. Gear and booking affiliates.

judgement.verdict: The data is excellent (NPS API plus open trail geometry supports thousands of genuinely distinct park, trail and waterfall pages), but most of the big volume sits in "near me" queries that are map-pack and app driven and that a static site rarely wins. The realistic prize is the long tail of park, trail and state pages, and the competition there (NPS.gov, AllTrails, Hiking Project-style aggregators) is stiff.

Target 'waterfalls near me' and state-level hike lists rather than the 'near me' head terms. Keep AI copy to short intros, and let the computed stats do most of the work.

pageTypes: /stay/[town]-vic: all accommodation in a town, with the computed attribute table
/stay/[town]-vic/[type]: e.g. hotels, B&Bs, cabins, caravan parks, per town (only where 10+ listings exist)
/stay-near/[landmark]-vic: e.g. stays near Great Ocean Road, Phillip Island Penguin Parade, Grampians (only where data is genuinely distinct)
Index hub /victoria/ with town list ranked by listing count and distance data
risks: Thin-content and scaled-content penalties: a list plus affiliate links with AI copy is exactly what Google's spam policies target; each page needs unique computed facts, not just generated prose
Booking.com and Expedia feed approval can take weeks and may reject a new site with little traffic
US search volume and USD CPC do not reflect Australian search; validate with Google Keyword Planner set to Australia
Brand-name queries (Lake House, Balgownie, Mantra) are controlled by the hotels and OTAs; targeting them invites trademark issues and gives no ranking chance
OSM data quality varies by town; rural listings can be stale or missing, causing empty or wrong pages
Crowded affiliate SERPs with Booking, Expedia, TripAdvisor, Wotif and Hotels.com; a small site competes on specificity, not authority
Seasonal demand (Victorian ski, coast and wine peaks) and low RPM make revenue lumpy
Booking.com affiliate terms restrict displaying prices or data outside their approved formats and can require caching limits; check before automating

idea: Victoria: where to eat by town
notes: Vic Tours. Restaurants by town. Data: OpenStreetMap (cuisine, hours). Weak affiliates; ads/leads.

judgement.verdict: Victorian restaurant data is thin and generic: OSM gives cuisine and hours, but no ratings, prices, menus or reviews, so pages would look like a directory that Google Maps already beats. The search volumes are US figures, which are unreliable for AU local intent, and the CPCs are low ($0.2–1.5), so revenue per page is tiny unless the site converts through affiliate tours or accommodation.
judgement.angle: A narrow Yarra Valley and Macedon Ranges winery-lunch guide (/winery-restaurants/[region]/ and /[winery]/ pages) built on OSM craft=winery and amenity=restaurant data, with a short factual card per venue and affiliate links for wine tours and stays. Skip general Geelong and Lorne 'best restaurants' pages until you have a real differentiator.
dataSources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API (amenity=restaurant/cafe, craft=winery, cuisine, opening_hours, website)
Victorian open data portals (data.vic.gov.au) for council and tourism datasets
Winery websites and official Yarra Valley / Macedon tourism listings (manual verification, not scraped at scale)
Google Places API only if you can afford its caching and display terms
monetisation: Viator (Tripadvisor affiliate) wine and food tours in the Yarra Valley
GetYourGuide Partner Program for experiences
Booking.com or Agoda affiliate (check current AU network) for accommodation near wineries
Klook for day trips and transfers
Display ads only once traffic justifies it; expect very low RPM at these CPCs
Lead-gen to private dining or group bookings, sold per enquiry to restaurants
pageTypes: /yarra-valley/[winery]/ (one page per winery, with real OSM facts and a verified lunch menu link)
/yarra-valley/lunch/[town]/ (Yarra Glen, Healesville, Lilydale, Coldstream)
/macedon-ranges/[town]-restaurants/ (Woodend, Hanging Rock, Daylesford hub links)
/tours/[region]/ tour comparison pages with affiliate tables
risks: US keyword volumes do not reflect Australian search demand; validate with AU keyword tools before building
OSM hours and cuisine tags are often missing or stale in regional Victoria; pages will look empty without manual checks
Thin AI-written copy over generic data is exactly what Google's helpful-content and spam policies target
ODbL licence: OSM data requires attribution and share-alike for any derived database you publish; check how your page output is treated
Google Places API terms restrict storing and caching place data, which undermines a bulk-generated site
Restaurants close or change hands often, so unmaintained pages decay quickly and can mislead diners
Low CPCs and small volumes mean the niche supports maybe a few thousand visits a month at best
